natural_body: Price-sensitive SMBs: 40% off drove signup +31%, revenue +18%, retention -12%.

first.rationale: Two independent inherited memories (memory_31, memory_86) converge on simplifying/shortening onboarding as a durable driver of activation and completion, which directly targets both declining metrics this quarter (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%). This is a controllable, internally-caused problem we can address with one experiment slot. The competitor's aggressive pricing move creates pressure to respond with promotional_pricing, but memory_73 already shows that discounting drove a 12% retention hit despite short-term revenue/signup gains — a direct conflict with the objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. I verified memory_73 to confirm that retention tradeoff is real before ruling out pricing as this week's play, and verified memory_86 to confirm the onboarding-shortening record is specific and not merely duplicative of memory_31's field-cutting experiment, since committing scarce experiment capacity to onboarding depends on these being genuinely reinforcing rather than the same single data point double-counted. I am not verifying enterprise_sales_assist or referral_incentive since neither addresses this quarter's acute metrics or the competitive threat as directly. Reactive discounting is deprioritized this cycle given its flagged downstream retention risk; onboarding fixes address root-cause activation/completion decay without sacrificing margin or retention. Scale is kept at standard_experiment rather than broad_rollout because current-quarter conditions (new competitor dynamics) are not fully captured by day-12/day-52 records, so full generalization is uncertain.
